name: MemTrapBench
ontology_notes: Eval of memory-induced cognitive traps, not a memory engine. User modeled is a multi-turn assistant doing puzzles, task switches, and safety queries. 1,050 instances. 350 Cognitive Bias, 350 Task Boundary, 200 Safety, 150 Trauma. Two categories are Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion. Final query is solvable without history. Metric is GPT-5.2 judge average of correctness, format, relevance, and efficiency. Correct retrieval can still be the wrong use. Traps are not typed retcon or a stored jailbreak of system persona. Trauma here is feedback-induced avoidance, a behavioral analogy, not companion trauma silence. Misses hole 1 identity drift after 50-plus sessions, hole 2 socially wrong timing of a known fact, hole 3 joke stored as relationship fact, hole 4 user retcon vs character lie vs narrator, hole 5 cross-character leak, hole 6 lorebook treated as lived event, hole 7 poisoned memory overrides system persona, hole 8 cost per turn, hole 9 forget-that, hole 10 three-month reunion.

supersession.evidence: Traps keep earlier memories valid in their original context. The failure is using them on the new query. No knowledge-update or fact-replacement category.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: History is multi-turn dialogue that plants a prior, then a final_trigger. No session timestamps, validity windows, or reunion queries.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One user talking to one model. Construction prompt mentions persona lock-in as a generation failure. There is no user vs character vs lore store.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Trauma (150) uses prior negative feedback so the model avoids a strategy that is correct now. Paper says Trauma is only a behavioral analogy. Task Boundary tests not carrying an old format across a task change. Neither is trauma/kink/spoiler silence on a known companion fact.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Safety (200) plants a counterfactual or sandbox premise and checks whether it overrides a straightforward safety judgment. Adjacent to hole 7. Not a stored jailbreak that overwrites a companion system persona. Cognitive Bias uses valid prior solutions as fixation, not planted malware.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that items. The correct behavior is to ignore an inapplicable but still-valid memory, not to delete it.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Efficiency is a judge axis for whether the answer uses a concise strategy. That is not tokens or LLM calls per turn.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Public GitHub tree with JSON instances and runners. No LICENSE file. GitHub license field is null. Judge is GPT-5.2. Consistency check uses Claude Sonnet 4.6.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Would prefer systems that can retrieve a relevant prior and still refuse to use it on the live query. That attacks retrieve-equals-remember. It would not select for character identity, RP lore, forget-that, or a planted overwrite of system persona.

published_eval.name: MemTrapBench
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper Table 1. Gemini-3-Flash-Preview wo/Mem average 85.16. Best memory strategy EverMemOS 71.17. Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 wo/Mem 81.83, LightMem 70.13. Abstract says even the strongest methods drop more than 10%. All listed memory strategies underperform no-memory. Table 3 Task Boundary trap average 31.05 vs no-trap 94.39.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether retrieved or in-context memory induces Reasoning Fixation (task boundary, cognitive bias, trauma-avoidance) or Belief Distortion (safety). Judge average of correctness, format, relevance, and efficiency. Final query is answerable without memory. Not companion identity or persona overwrite.
